subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default model-facing behavior, and what explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain for agents that need complete page state or refs?
rationale: The code already has efficient snapshot options and general tool-output caps, but changing the default browser read contract affects agent behavior, refs, context quality, and compatibility with existing browser workflows.

options.title: Compact Default With Raw Escape Hatch
options.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads the default, keep an explicit full/ARIA/raw snapshot path, and require live noisy-page proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep Config-Only Efficient Mode
options.body: Leave efficient mode as an opt-in configuration and close only if maintainers decide the current documented configuration is sufficient.

options.title: Track Under Broader Browser Field Work
options.body: Move the remaining work into the open browser field-report cluster if maintainers prefer one canonical browser automation quality plan.

recommendation.title: Compact Default With Raw Escape Hatch
recommendation.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads the default, keep an explicit full/ARIA/raw snapshot path, and require live noisy-page proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin runtime extraction and owner-boundary history make this the strongest available maintainer-routing signal for deciding the browser tool contract.
